manifest.name: Payment Provider: Custom Payment Modes
manifest.summary: A payment provider for custom flows like wire transfers.
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models._description: Payment Provider (Custom mode: wire_transfer; optional QR code display)
relations: qr_code (Boolean: Enable QR Codes for wire transfer)

models._description: Payment Transaction (Custom: always set to pending; no real payment network involved)
relations: no new fields; 6 methods overriding payment rendering/processing/messaging hooks

security.note: No own ACL/rules; relies on payment's security. DB constraint: CHECK(custom_mode IS NULL OR (code = 'custom' AND custom_mode IS NOT NULL)).

views.note: xml_loc=175: payment.provider form inheritance (custom_mode + qr_code fields), QWeb pending_msg template rendering bank account details. No own model views.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._get_specific_rendering_values -> api_url=CustomController._process_url + reference; _apply_updates -> _set_pending unconditionally; _extract_amount_data -> None (skips amount validation)
behavioral_notes.observation: Unlike real online acquirers, payment_custom implements an offline/manual flow. _get_specific_rendering_values returns only {api_url: '/payment/custom/process', reference: self.reference}; there is no redirect to a payment gateway. The QWeb template renders a form that POSTs to /payment/custom/process. CustomController.custom_process_transaction (csrf=False, public, POST) does nothing except call payment.transaction.sudo()._process('custom', post) and redirect to /payment/status. _apply_updates (the hook called by _process) unconditionally calls self._set_pending() -- the transaction is always placed in 'pending' state regardless of what POST data is received. _extract_amount_data returns None for provider_code=='custom', instructing the payment engine to skip amount validation entirely. This means no funds movement is tracked, no API call is ever made, and the transaction settles to 'pending' only -- it never advances to 'done' via this module. All of this deliberate no-op flow is invisible from model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: post_processing.js: PaymentPostProcessing patch adds 'pending' to getFinalStates for 'custom' provider so the post-processing page redirects immediately rather than polling
behavioral_notes.observation: The standard payment post-processing page polls transaction state until a terminal state (done/error/canceled) is reached. For 'custom' providers, transactions stay in 'pending' forever because _apply_updates never calls _set_done. Without the JS patch, the post-processing page would poll indefinitely. static/src/interactions/post_processing.js patches PaymentPostProcessing.getFinalStates: when providerCode === 'custom', 'pending' is added to the finalStates set, causing the post-processing widget to treat 'pending' as a terminal state and redirect to the landing route immediately. This client-side patch is the only thing that makes the user experience coherent for offline/manual payment flows, and it is entirely invisible from Python metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.provider.action_recompute_pending_msg -> builds HTML pending_msg from account.journal bank accounts when account_payment module is installed; _transfer_ensure_pending_msg_is_set auto-triggers it
behavioral_notes.observation: The wire-transfer pending_msg (the payment instructions shown to the customer after they submit) is dynamically built from the company's bank accounts. action_recompute_pending_msg checks whether the account_payment module is installed (ir.module.module._get('account_payment').state == 'installed'); if yes, it searches account.journal records of type='bank' for the provider's company, collects their bank_account_id.display_name values, and assembles an HTML block listing them with a 'Please use the following transfer details' header. _transfer_ensure_pending_msg_is_set is called to auto-invoke this when pending_msg is empty. The create() override also nullifies pending_msg immediately after creation for wire_transfer providers so it gets freshly computed. The dependency on account_payment and the dynamic bank-account lookup are completely invisible from field/model metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._get_communication -> returns invoice payment_reference or sale order reference or tx.reference for wire transfers; _get_sent_message -> custom message; _log_received_message -> suppressed for custom
behavioral_notes.observation: _get_communication builds the communication string the customer should include in their bank transfer: it checks for invoice_ids (uses invoice_ids[0].payment_reference) then sale_order_ids (uses sale_order_ids[0].reference) and falls back to self.reference. This allows the merchant to match incoming bank transfers to the right Odoo document by payment reference. _get_sent_message returns 'The customer has selected {provider_name} to make the payment.' instead of the generic acquirer message. _log_received_message is overridden to exclude custom transactions from the chatter message (filtered out before calling super), because custom providers do not actually 'receive' a notification from any external system -- logging a received message would be misleading. These three messaging overrides tailor the UX for an offline flow and are invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.provider DB constraint + _get_provider_domain + custom_mode selection extensibility design
behavioral_notes.observation: A PostgreSQL CHECK constraint (_custom_providers_setup: 'CHECK(custom_mode IS NULL OR (code = custom AND custom_mode IS NOT NULL))') enforces that only providers with code='custom' may have a non-null custom_mode, and that custom providers must have a custom_mode set. Currently only one custom_mode value exists: 'wire_transfer'. _get_provider_domain is overridden: when provider_code=='custom' and a custom_mode keyword argument is provided, it ANDs a ('custom_mode', '=', custom_mode) domain clause so callers can locate a specific custom provider variant. _get_removal_values nullifies custom_mode when a provider is removed/reset. This design allows future custom_mode values (e.g. 'check', 'cash') to be added without schema changes. The constraint and domain extension are invisible to field/model metadata.

it_architecture.application: payment_custom (manual/offline payment adapter for the payment engine; no external API; _inherit-only, no own models)
software_services: /payment/custom/process (http, public, POST, csrf=False: receives the submitted payment form; calls _process('custom', post) -> _set_pending; redirects to /payment/status)
data_objects: payment.provider (+code='custom', custom_mode='wire_transfer', qr_code; DB constraint enforces custom_mode not null for code='custom')
payment.transaction (offline/manual flow; always -> pending; no new fields)
logical_data_erm: payment.transaction -> payment.provider (provider_id; provider_code=='custom' gates every override)
payment.provider.custom_mode (Selection: wire_transfer; extensible for future modes)
payment.provider.pending_msg (HTML; dynamically built from account.journal bank accounts when account_payment installed)
external reference: payment.transaction._get_communication -> invoice payment_reference or sale order reference (cross-document reconciliation hint for the bank)
information_flows: optional integration: account_payment module (checked at runtime to build bank-account pending_msg; not a declared depends)
inbound (form submit): browser -> /payment/custom/process POST -> _process('custom', post) -> _set_pending -> redirect /payment/status
side-effect: action_recompute_pending_msg queries account.journal (bank type, company-scoped) to build wire transfer instructions HTML
no outbound API calls: payment_custom makes zero HTTP calls to external systems (uses_api_keys=false, endpoints=[])
frontend_components: PaymentPostProcessing (patch; adds 'pending' to getFinalStates for 'custom' provider so the post-processing page treats pending as terminal and redirects immediately rather than polling)

external_integrations.pattern: Deliberately no external integration: payment_custom is an offline/manual provider. There are no outbound API calls, no SDKs, no webhooks, and no external payment network. The gap #7 surface is empty by design. The only 'integration' is the optional runtime check for the account_payment module to populate bank account details.

capabilities: Accept offline / manual payments via wire transfer (bank transfer) with customer-facing instructions listing company bank accounts
Generate a communication/reference string for bank reconciliation (invoice payment_reference or sale order reference)
Display QR codes on the wire-transfer instructions page (qr_code flag; rendered by upstream payment QWeb template)
Support any future custom payment mode via the extensible custom_mode Selection field without schema changes
Adapt the post-processing experience to offline flows: treat 'pending' as final for custom providers (no polling)
value_streams: Collect-Payment (wire transfer, offline): customer selects Custom provider -> _get_specific_rendering_values -> pending_msg with bank account details displayed -> customer submits form -> POST /payment/custom/process -> _set_pending -> /payment/status (pending treated as final by JS patch) -> accountant manually reconciles incoming bank transfer
Reconcile: _get_communication returns invoice/sale reference -> customer includes reference in bank transfer -> accountant matches transfer to invoice/order
information_concepts: payment.provider (custom code; custom_mode=wire_transfer; qr_code; pending_msg HTML with bank account details)
payment.transaction (offline payment intent; always pending; reference used as bank transfer communication)
account.journal bank accounts (queried dynamically to build pending_msg; owned by account_payment module)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; relies entirely on payment's groups and record rules)
policies: Transaction always lands in 'pending': _apply_updates unconditionally calls _set_pending; no done/error/canceled path exists in this module
Amount validation skipped: _extract_amount_data returns None for 'custom' so the payment engine skips amount reconciliation (no API response to validate against)
DB integrity: PostgreSQL CHECK constraint ensures custom_mode is set if and only if code='custom'

Pending message auto-recomputed: wire_transfer providers with empty pending_msg auto-trigger action_recompute_pending_msg via _transfer_ensure_pending_msg_is_set; create() nullifies pending_msg on creation to force a fresh compute
Chatter suppressed: _log_received_message excludes custom transactions (no real external notification received)
Post-processing polls: PaymentPostProcessing JS patch adds 'pending' to finalStates for 'custom' so the browser does not poll indefinitely
stakeholders: Payer / Customer (res.partner; sees wire-transfer instructions and reference in the portal)
Merchant / Company (res.company; owns the bank accounts listed in the instructions)
Accountant (manually reconciles incoming bank transfers against pending payment.transactions using the communication reference)
System Administrator (configures custom provider, custom_mode, bank accounts)
metrics: (no own reports; pending transaction counts surfaced by the parent payment.transaction pivot/graph; accountant must manually track reconciliation)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; offline wire-transfer collection)
classification.rationale: payment_custom is classified as value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) because it mediates between the payer and the merchant -- specifically by providing the payment instructions and reference that allow an offline bank transfer to be matched to an Odoo transaction. It is a degenerate case of a network: there is no real-time external network call, but the module's structural role in the payment engine is identical to other acquirers (it is a 'code=custom' selection_add provider, extends payment.provider and payment.transaction, and plugs into the same payment flow). activity_class is 'support' because offline payment collection is a finance/administrative support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False) under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash via wire transfer.

standard_capabilities: wire-transfer payment instructions with dynamic bank account listing (requires account_payment for account.journal lookup)
QR code display on wire-transfer instructions (qr_code flag)
bank-reconciliation communication reference (invoice payment_reference or sale order reference or tx reference)
extensible custom_mode Selection for future offline payment types without schema change
post-processing UX adapted for offline flows (pending treated as terminal, no polling)
typical_fits: B2B merchants accepting bank transfers / wire transfers (e.g. invoicing with deferred payment)
markets where online card acceptance is not practical or available
any scenario where payment intent is recorded in Odoo but settlement happens outside the system
common_gaps: transaction never advances past 'pending' automatically: the accountant must manually match and confirm each bank transfer
no automated bank reconciliation or SEPA import integration in this module; downstream account_payment module handles that
no real-time payment confirmation: there is no webhook or API callback, so the customer experience ends at 'pending'
only one custom_mode currently (wire_transfer); other offline modes (check, cash) would require extending the Selection and adding new pending_msg logic
qr_code display depends on upstream payment QWeb templates and downstream bank-account QR generation; this module only sets the flag

pending_msg HTML is generated at configuration time, not at transaction time, so if bank accounts change after providers are configured the message can become stale unless action_recompute_pending_msg is re-run
drive_hints: odoo shell: p=env['payment.provider'].search([('code','=','custom'),('custom_mode','=','wire_transfer')],limit=1); print(p.pending_msg[:200] if p.pending_msg else 'empty')
curl -X POST https://<host>/payment/custom/process (public, csrf=False) with reference=<ref> -> expect redirect to /payment/status with tx in 'pending' state

open_questions: How does the accountant operationally confirm and close a pending wire-transfer transaction in Odoo -- is there a manual 'mark as paid' action in account_payment, or does it happen via bank statement import/reconciliation?
The qr_code flag is set here but the actual QR rendering is upstream; which QWeb template consumes it and what format (SEPA QR, Swiss QR bill, generic URL QR)?
Are there plans to add more custom_mode values (e.g. 'check', 'cash_on_delivery')? The extensibility design is in place but no values other than 'wire_transfer' exist.
pending_msg can become stale if bank accounts are added/removed after provider configuration; is there a server action or cron that keeps it fresh?
Real-world transaction volume and pending-to-reconciled conversion rate (no runtime row counts captured).
